one_liner: D-written single-threaded BLAS GEMM that beat OpenBLAS 0.2.18 by 10-15% in 2016; abandoned since 2018.
what_it_does: Mir GLAS is a static C library written in D (betterC, no D or C++ runtime needed beyond libc) that exports the Fortran BLAS symbols (sgemm_, dgemm_, cgemm_, zgemm_, ?symm_, ?hemm_ and Level 1) plus its own GLAS API, in which a matrix is passed as an ndslice struct of two lengths, two strides and a pointer. CBLAS is only available by linking Netlib's CBLAS on top. Only GEMM, SYMM, HEMM and Level 1 are implemented; TRSM, TRMM, SYRK and all of Level 2 are missing. It links against mir-cpuid for cache detection.
how_it_is_fast: It is a Goto-style packed GEMM: A and B are packed into contiguous panels, and a register-blocked micro-kernel accumulates an mr x nr tile of C using LLVM vector types, without assembler. One generic kernel serves float, double and both complex types; the register-blocking shape comes from a small per-ISA configuration (x87, SSE2, AVX/AVX2, AVX-512F) chosen at compile time with __traits(targetHasFeature). Block sizes kc and mc are computed at runtime from the L1 and last-level cache sizes reported by mir-cpuid. The author also argues that the kernels are not unrolled, so they put less pressure on the instruction cache.
when_to_use: Reading or porting a compact, assembler-free generic GEMM design (one kernel for real and complex types, a per-ISA register-blocking table) as a reference.
Single-threaded GEMM on small square matrices (n <= 100) on an Intel Haswell-class CPU, where the 2016 data show the largest margin over OpenBLAS 0.2.18 (median about 1.4x for sgemm and dgemm).
Single-threaded complex GEMM where the alternative is Eigen 3.3 or Apple Accelerate: the 2016 data show about 1.9x over Eigen and about 3.3x over Accelerate for cgemm and zgemm.
D projects already pinned to an old LDC and mir-algorithm 0.x that want a dependency-light BLAS with an ndslice interface.
when_not_to_use: Any multithreaded workload: multithreading is an unchecked item in the README, while OpenBLAS and MKL scale across cores.

Current toolchains: the README warns of open issue #18, a 2x GEMM slowdown when built with LLVM 4.x-5.x versus 3.9.1, and the build prints a 'PERFORMANCE NOTE: LLVM >=4.0 has a bug in register renaming' and falls back to a smaller kernel. Issue #29 (open since June 2018) says a release is needed for mir-algorithm > 0.9.0, and issue #22 reports dub failing to build it with its dependencies.
AMD CPUs: open issue #20 (April 2017) reports it slower than OpenBLAS and ACML for DGEMM on an AMD machine, with no maintainer reply.
Large double-precision GEMM where Intel MKL is available: in the author's own data MKL is ahead on dgemm and zgemm at every size from about 500 to 2000.
Code needing a full BLAS: TRSM, TRMM, SYRK, SYR2K, HERK and all Level 2 routines are missing, so LAPACK cannot sit on top of it alone.

integration.form: static lib (built with dub and LDC; a dynamic configuration exists in dub.json but the README lists shared-library support as unfinished)
integration.dependencies: mir-cpuid (link order -lmir-glas -lmir-cpuid); mir-algorithm for the D headers; Netlib CBLAS if you want the CBLAS interface
integration.min_toolchain: LDC >= 1.1.0 beta 6 (README); built with ldmd2, -betterC and -mcpu=native for the target-native build; works with C99 callers via include/glas/*.h. Builds with current LDC releases are not documented.
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 (register configurations for x87, SSE2, AVX/AVX2, AVX-512F); POSIX and Windows memory back-ends; other targets need a mir-cpuid port and a new configuration
integration.thread_safety: Not documented, and not safe from code reading: glas_init and the GEMM blocking routine use process-global __gshared state, including one shared pack buffer that each call reuses or reallocates, so concurrent calls from several threads race on it.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it exports the Fortran BLAS symbols for gemm, symm, hemm and Level 1 only; CBLAS needs Netlib's CBLAS wrapper, and every other BLAS routine is absent

gotchas: The ISA kernel is fixed at compile time (__traits(targetHasFeature), -mcpu=native in the target-native build), so a library built on an AVX-512 machine is not safe to ship to older CPUs, and there is no runtime dispatch.

The C header include/glas/ndslice.h declares glas_zaxpy and _glas_zaxpy with a float _Complex alpha, while the D implementation takes cdouble; C or C++ callers of zaxpy through that header pass alpha with the wrong type.
The README ticks 'CI testing with Netlib's BLAS test suite', but in .travis.yml the test.sh step that runs the Netlib CBLAS tests is commented out; CI only builds the gemm and hemm examples.
Call glas_release() to free the shared pack buffer; otherwise it stays allocated at its largest size for the life of the process.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: Laser is the closest sibling (same era, also stale, but multithreaded and at parity with modern OpenBLAS), and BLASFEO is the maintained choice for small matrices. Pick Mir GLAS only to study a generic, assembler-free GEMM kernel design or for single-threaded complex GEMM in an old D toolchain.
verified_claims_summary: The author's 2016 single-thread benchmark on a 2.2 GHz i7-4770HQ MacBook Pro (Mir GLAS 0.18.0 built with LDC, version and flags unstated) against OpenBLAS 0.2.18, Eigen 3.3-rc1, MKL 2017.0.098 and Accelerate for m=n=k from 10 to 2000 gives median Mir/OpenBLAS ratios of 1.15x sgemm, 1.13x dgemm, 1.12x cgemm and 1.10x zgemm; the margin is largest at n <= 100 (median about 1.4x for real types) and shrinks to about 1.03x for dgemm at n >= 500, and MKL is roughly equal (ratios derived from page data). The benchmark source (libmir/mir benchmarks/glas/gemm_report.d) is gone, and the numbers predate the LLVM 4 slowdown reported in issue #18.
status_note: Abandoned: the last code change was in mid-2018 and the last commit a README edit in August 2022; Boost-licensed and small, but it needs an old LDC/LLVM to reproduce the published speed.
